name: Ming-Qing Street Core
tagline: The living heart of the walled Ancient City
description: The central spine of the old town, where restored shopfronts, the Rishengchang draft bank, teahouses and guildhalls line grey-stone lanes. It is the most atmospheric and most touristed stretch inside the walls, busy by day and lantern-lit by night, packed with heritage in every direction.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want to sleep amid the heritage
pros: Steps from major sights and the draft bank
Lively evening atmosphere with red lanterns
cons: Very crowded and touristy by day
Noisier and pricier than quieter lanes

name: South Gate (Yingxun) Area
tagline: Grand entrance by the ancient walls
description: Clustered around the southern Yingxun Gate, this area is many visitors' first impression of Pingyao, with sweeping views of the Ming-dynasty walls and easy wall-climbing access. Guesthouses and eateries gather here, making it a convenient, scenic base close to the ramparts.
bestFor: Travelers who want wall views and easy access in and out
pros: Dramatic city-wall views on your doorstep
Handy for entering and leaving the old town
Plenty of dining and lodging nearby
cons: Tour groups cluster at the gate
Can feel like a transit point

name: Quiet Residential Lanes
tagline: Everyday life behind the tourist streets
description: Step a few blocks off the main axis and the Ancient City turns residential, with hushed grey-brick lanes, local courtyard homes, small shops and the rhythms of daily life. These quieter blocks offer a calmer, more authentic slice of Pingyao while staying inside the historic walls.
bestFor: Slow travelers wanting quiet inside the old town
pros: Cheaper guesthouse rates than the core

name: New Town and Rail Station
tagline: Modern Pingyao and the high-speed gateway
description: Outside the walls lies the ordinary modern town, with wider roads, taxis, DiDi, supermarkets and the Pingyao Ancient City high-speed rail station connecting to Taiyuan, Xian and Beijing. It lacks the old town's charm but offers practicality, transport links and everyday conveniences.
bestFor: Those prioritizing transport links and modern amenities
pros: High-speed rail access to major cities
cons: A short trip from the walled sights
